the density of periumoral lymphatic vessels and lymphatic invasion is an independent prognostic factor in cutaneous melanoma, while the VEGF is not.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lymphatic invasion and the ulceration are more reliable predictors for metastasis of melanoma to the sentinel lymph nodes.
the lymphatic vessels are present in both SLN positive and SLN negative patients, but the lymphatic invasion is a sign of a potential for the metastasis.

the density of intratunmoral and peritunmoral lymphatic vessels is low up to moderate at both SLN positive and SLN negative patients, and the lymphatic vessels are absent in the group of the SLN negative patients in all p T stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lymphatic invasion is the most reliable predictor of the melanoma metastasis.
the lymphatic invasion is the most important prognostic factor in the metastasis of cutaneous melanomas.
the VEGF plays an important role in the lymphangiogenesis in melanomas, and the lymphatic vessels in the peritumoral area are not a reliable indicator of the metastatic potential of the melanoma.
